report.source_text: Our patient is an 82-year-old Caucasian female with a lifetime non-smoking history who presented to our institution with generalized fatigue, fever, night sweats, cough, and pleuritic chest pain. She had no significant comorbidities, was retired and lived with her partner. She had recently traveled to the western part of the United States. Additionally, she had recently undergone periodontal deep cleaning with no peri-procedural antibiotics. Laboratory testing was significant for a leukocytosis of 13.5 white blood cells per microliter and a viral panel negative for respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and coronavirus disease 2019.

report.source_text: Biopsy revealed pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (Fig. 3, Fig. 4). The mass demonstrated a high-grade, malignant spindle cell proliferation with occasional multinucleated giant cells and inter-lesional acute and chronic inflammation. Immunostains demonstrated the tumor cells to be diffusely positive for low molecular weight cytokeratin Cam 5.2.

report.source_text: Surgical consult was obtained, but the decision was made to defer surgery given the transdiaphragmatic invasion. She was begun on systemic chemotherapy with a platinum-based regimen. On follow-up 3 weeks later, she was tolerating treatment without complication.

clinician.trajectory_summary: 82-year-old lifetime non-smoking female presented with systemic symptoms including fatigue, fever, night sweats, cough, and pleuritic chest pain. Labs showed leukocytosis of 13.5 x10^3/μL, and respiratory viral panel was negative. Imaging revealed a large heterogeneous mass extending from the right pulmonary hilum to liver segments VII and VIII without distant metastases. CT-guided biopsy confirmed pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma characterized by high-grade spindle cell proliferation with cytokeratin Cam 5.2 positivity. PET scan showed no additional disease. Surgical resection was deferred due to transdiaphragmatic invasion, and patient started on platinum-based systemic chemotherapy, with good tolerance at 3-week follow-up.

CT-guided biopsy confirming pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma with high-grade spindle cell tumor and cytokeratin positivity
PET scan showing no additional disease
Treatment with systemic platinum-based chemotherapy after decision against surgery due to invasion; good tolerance at follow-up
